findings.text: The first lede tells a newcomer what Athena is in plain words. After that, the page says almost nothing more about Athena itself, and the only demo of it is this study.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost."

findings.text: This is the root URL of Athena's site, but the title and almost all of the content are about a different project, firstmate. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena may be confused about which project the page is for.
findings.source: <title>Athena explains how firstmate handles work</title> / h1 of the same text

findings.text: This gives a clear reason the page exists: every statement can be traced to a source. The claim ids, which link to line ranges at a fixed commit, back that up throughout the page.
findings.source: "Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim, and every claim to lines in the project's own files."

findings.text: The page links to next steps right at the top. The Next steps section gives the repo link, an install command and a sample request, so the reader knows what to do.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and the Next steps section

findings.text: The install step assumes the reader already has a checkout. There is no clone command, and the page does not say what setup.sh needs or what you get after running it.
findings.source: "Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh"

findings.text: The walkthrough meant for newcomers uses words it hasn't explained yet. 'Unheld' is never defined, and exit codes show up in step 2. This makes the start-to-finish story hard to follow on a first read.
findings.source: Start here > One piece of work: "A spawn is accepted only for an unheld, unblocked item." / "the spawn exits 75"

findings.text: Someone who came for firstmate gets a clear answer about what it is and what problem it solves, and it comes before the detailed sections.
findings.source: Start here > What firstmate is: "Firstmate is a tool for people who direct AI coding agents... so that several tasks can run side by side without the workers overwriting each other's files"

findings.text: Many definitions appear two or three times: in the 'Words used first' list, again in the Glossary, and again inside the cards. This makes the page longer and denser than a first-time reader needs.
findings.source: Words used first, Glossary, and Transitions cards (e.g. "in scope" defined identically in both lists)

findings.text: The page says plainly that the study only read firstmate's files and never ran it. This helps a newcomer judge how far to trust what the page says.
findings.source: Limits of this study: "every claim is marked read" / "no run confirmed that a script behaves as its header says"
